metadata.title: They Were Paying the CIA
metadata.global_visual_style: Historical archival photo style, Kodachrome 60s–80s film grain, cinematic noir lighting, high-contrast shadows, desaturated Cold War palette with occasional bursts of amber and blue. 9:16 vertical framing. Fast cuts — visual change every 3 seconds minimum.
metadata.bg_music_note: No background music. Intentional — maximizes Shorts revenue pool allocation. All audio is narration and SFX only.
metadata.duration_note: ~10 words per narration line at 2.2 words/sec = ~4.5s per scene. 12 scenes + 2s hook + 4s loop = ~55s total.

timeline.visual_description: Black screen. Large white sans-serif text snaps in: 'THEY WERE PAYING THE CIA.' Cold, stark. 9:16 vertical frame.

timeline.narration: 120 governments paid a Swiss company to keep their secrets.
timeline.visual_description: Vintage documentary-style world map, Europe centered, Switzerland highlighted with a soft golden pulse. Kodachrome warm tones on aged parchment-texture map.
CIA seal fills the frame, over-exposed, institutional. Flat, cold morning light.

timeline.narration: Iran. Argentina. The Vatican. Pakistan. India.
timeline.visual_description: Rapid staccato montage — each national flag fills frame for half a second: Iran, Argentina, Vatican City, Pakistan, India. Flat dark background, Kodachrome grain.
timeline.sfx_prompt: each flag cut lands with a quiet sharp percussive tick

timeline.narration: Every message they sent — the CIA could read it.
timeline.visual_description: Extreme close-up of a mechanical cipher machine — brass rotors, key switches. Hands pressing keys. Warm amber light on metal. Kodachrome grain.
timeline.sfx_prompt: rhythmic mechanical key presses, cipher rotor clicks

timeline.narration: The encryption looked real. The backdoor was built in from the start.
timeline.visual_description: Split screen — left: diplomat transmitting a cable; right: CIA analyst reading the decoded printout. Cinematic noir, 1970s institutional interiors.
timeline.sfx_prompt: faint teletype machine, quiet office ambient

timeline.narration: Falklands War. Britain knew every Argentine move in real time.
timeline.visual_description: Archival-style photograph of Argentine naval vessels at sea — grey water, overcast sky, military silhouettes. Desaturated Kodachrome, slight vignette.
timeline.sfx_prompt: distant ocean wind, faint ship engine hum

timeline.visual_description: Overhead shot of towering stacks of classified documents. Top folder bears a heavy red CLASSIFIED stamp. Single hard overhead light, everything else in shadow.

timeline.narration: Exposed in 2020 by the Washington Post.
timeline.visual_description: Washington Post front page, February 2020, laid on a dark surface. Overhead camera, hard light source. Kodachrome warm paper tones.

timeline.narration: 'The intelligence coup of the century.' — CIA's own words.
timeline.visual_description: Close-up of a declassified document page. The phrase highlighted in bright yellow marker. Slow push-in zoom. Aged paper, Kodachrome cream tones.

timeline.narration: He made a gentleman's agreement with the CIA in 1951.
timeline.visual_description: Black and white photograph of Boris Hagelin — older gentleman in a business suit, 1950s formal portrait. Kodachrome warm overlay converts to soft sepia.
Channel-branded card — the Crypto AG documentary thumbnail with bold text overlay: 'FULL STORY: 26 MINUTES'. Chronicles of Eras channel name. Dark background.
LOOP SETUP — identical to opening frame: Black screen. White text: 'THEY WERE PAYING THE CIA.' Holds for 4 seconds. Seamless replay trigger.
